title: Les Patriotes du Nord security meeting in Ouahigouya
location: Place de la Nation, Ouahigouya, North Region
scope: Local public meeting addressing regional and national security
participants_original: LeFaso describes the square as crowded and residents as turning out in large numbers; no numeric count is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Qualitative evidence: LeFaso describes the Place de la Nation as crowded and attendees as turning out en masse. The report supports an assessment of at least 50 people but gives no numeric estimate; no count is inferred.

start_date.summary: The contemporaneous article states the meeting occurred Sunday 15 January 2023.

end_date.summary: Article says attendees returned home around noon after the meeting.

location.summary: Place de la Nation in Ouahigouya, North Region.

organizer.summary: Meeting organized by Les Patriotes du Nord.

demands.summary: Organizer focused on worsening insecurity, called for recruitment into local defense groups and explicitly asked authorities to arm the population; other appeals were directed to merchants and business owners.

participants_original.summary: Reporter describes the square as crowded and turnout as large; no number is stated.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative crowded-square and mass-turnout descriptions support the agent assessment that the public gathering exceeded 50; no count or numerical bound is claimed.

protester_violence.summary: Article does not establish whether any violence occurred; remains unknown.

state_response.summary: S018 says authorities contacted organizers before the 15 January meeting, wanted it cancelled because they had received the concerns, and promised significant responses. S019, by the same LeFaso reporter, retrospectively says actions by FDS/VDP under transition authorities followed the appeal, including resupply to Titao and Sollé. This supports reported accommodation, not verified policy success or independent corroboration.

notes: The local meeting raised insecurity and asked domestic authorities to arm residents; only this explicit domestic-policy demand supports the state-target test. The distinct appeal to merchants and business owners is not evidence of a state demand. The organizer warned of a possible future march if security did not improve; that prospective action is not coded. The meeting went ahead after authorities reportedly asked for cancellation. The only source opened for this candidate is one local report; AIB search-result attendance language remains unverified after a technical Cache miss. A 29 January LeFaso follow-up by the same reporter says security actions followed the 15 January appeal and supplies reached Titao and Sollé; this is same-outlet reporting, not independent corroboration.
open_questions: No numeric attendance estimate; the AIB exact-URL body attempt returned Cache miss.
Protester violence and other state responses are not reported.
Independent review, official baseline and episode reconciliation remain pending.
Reported post-appeal security actions are only from same-outlet LeFaso follow-up; independent verification and outcomes remain unresolved.

title: CLP anti-France demonstration in Ouagadougou
organizer: Collectif des Leaders Panafricains (CLP), described as grouping several civil-society organizations
participants_original: Anadolu Agency reports “several hundred” demonstrators; no exact count.
threshold_50_evidence: Anadolu Agency reports several hundred people in the streets of Ouagadougou, an attributed qualitative estimate supporting the >=50 threshold; no exact numerical bound is inferred.

start_date.summary: Report describes the demonstration on Friday 20 January 2023.

location.summary: Demonstrators took to streets in Ouagadougou; no narrower site is stated.

organizer.summary: Participants answered the call of the CLP, which the report says groups civil-society organizations.

demands.summary: Explicit requests were the departure of the French ambassador and dismantling of the French Sabre force. One attendee also said they came out to support the transition president as he stood up to France.

participants_original.summary: Anadolu Agency states several hundred demonstrators; no exact number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Attributed report of several hundred supports the threshold qualitatively.

protester_violence.summary: Article does not establish protester violence; remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Article does not report a state response to this gathering; all response variables remain unknown.

notes: The opened report directs explicit demands to France. An attendee expressed support for Ibrahim Traore, but the report does not establish an explicit request directed to Burkina Faso authorities or a domestic policy demand. Foreign diplomatic context and later state actions are not used to infer the crowd target. Local, date-specific assembly is distinct from the 28 January meeting.
open_questions: Does contemporaneous reporting show an explicit demand to Burkina Faso authorities or a domestic policy request at this assembly?
Physical end and state response are not reported.
Independent review, official baseline and episode reconciliation remain pending.

title: Ouagadougou meeting supporting the transition and French troop withdrawal
scope: Local meeting; source also reports simultaneous mobilizations in other cities without resolving their sites or relationship
organizer: Civil-society organizations; CLP is identified as a participating organizer
participants_original: Burkina24 reports thousands of people; no exact count.
threshold_50_evidence: Burkina24 describes thousands at the meeting, supporting the >=50 threshold as a qualitative reported estimate; no numerical bounds are inferred.

start_date.summary: Burkina24 dates the meeting to Saturday 28 January 2023.

location.summary: Place de la Nation in Ouagadougou.

organizer.summary: The article says civil-society organizations organized the meeting and names CLP as a member of the organizing group.

demands.summary: Participants expressed support for the transition and authorities’ decisions, including the policy to withdraw the French military base and choices about security cooperation. A CLP representative said their demand for French forces to leave had received government support; this is evidence of explicit support for domestic policy at the meeting, not a claim that the earlier Jan 20 event caused the government decision.

participants_original.summary: Burkina24 describes thousands attending; no exact count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative report of thousands at an assembled meeting supports >=50.

protester_violence.summary: An organizer describes the mobilization as peaceful; this is attributed and does not establish state response.

state_response.summary: The article refers to a government decision to withdraw the French base as a policy supported by participants, but does not establish that this specific Jan 28 meeting elicited a state response. All seven event response fields remain unknown.

notes: Domestic policy target is supported by explicit statements backing authorities’ decisions and security-cooperation choices at this meeting. Its support is not exclusively electoral or party-political in the source. The report says similar mobilizations took place simultaneously in many cities; those sites are not enumerated here. The French withdrawal deadline is reported as an existing government decision and is not assigned as a response to this particular Jan 28 meeting or to the Jan 20 gathering. Keep this physical assembly distinct pending review from the same-day Bobo-Dioulasso report and earlier CLP action.
open_questions: The article says mobilizations occurred simultaneously in many cities; their locations and whether they were one nationally organized episode are unresolved.
Physical end and any event-specific state response are not reported.
Independent review, official baseline and episode reconciliation remain pending.

title: Bobo-Dioulasso meeting supporting the transition
organizer: Civil-society group calling itself the Movement in Support of the Transition, FDS and VDP
participants_original: No crowd count or general attendance estimate is reported. The article mentions a parade of about ten horsemen; this is not a count of meeting participants.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Burkina24 confirms the meeting but gives no participant count or general crowd-size description; the approximately ten horsemen mentioned are not the crowd.

start_date.summary: Burkina24 says the group held the meeting Saturday 28 January 2023.

organizer.summary: A group of civil-society organizations identifying as Movement in Support of the Transition, FDS and VDP.

demands.summary: Report records support for transition and Ibrahim Traore, a warning to the Ivorian president against interference in the transition process, and a local speaker appealing that Bobo not be neglected; the appeal’s addressee and fit to a domestic state policy demand are uncertain.

participants_original.summary: No attendance estimate. About ten horsemen are mentioned in a parade, which is not crowd size.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No evidence establishing at least 50 attendees.

protester_violence.summary: Article does not describe protester violence; remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Article does not report responses by Burkina Faso state forces or authorities.

notes: Do not count the ten horsemen as total attendance. The Bobo article separately references a Ouagadougou meeting the same day; Burkina24 Ouagadougou reporting also says gatherings occurred simultaneously in other cities. Relation to that report remains unresolved; no automatic merge or shared attendance is assumed.
open_questions: Whether turnout reached 50 is unknown.
Whether the appeal for Bobo not to be neglected was directed to Burkina Faso authorities and met the domestic policy target is unresolved; the warning to Côte d’Ivoire alone is foreign-directed.
Relationship to the Ouagadougou meeting and broader simultaneous mobilizations is not established.
Physical end and state responses are unreported.

title: Patriotes du Nord follow-up meeting on security in Ouahigouya
location: Place de la Nation, Ouahigouya, North Region
scope: Local meeting with regional security focus
participants_original: LeFaso describes an immense crowd and attendees as turning out en masse; no numeric count is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Qualitative evidence: LeFaso describes an immense crowd, mass turnout and representation from several provinces. This supports the >=50 threshold, but the article gives no numeric estimate and no number is inferred.

start_date.summary: LeFaso states the meeting took place Saturday 28 January 2023.

end_date.summary: LeFaso says participants returned home around 13:00 after a three-hour meeting.

location.summary: Place de la Nation in Ouahigouya.

organizer.summary: Meeting called by Les Patriotes du Nord.

demands.summary: Meeting thanks transition authorities for reported security actions after the 15 January appeal, invites authorities to greater engagement, and calls for mass enrollment in VDP. Also demands French army departure; this foreign-directed demand is not the sole domestic-state target evidence.

participants_original.summary: The report describes an immense crowd and mass turnout without a numeric count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative description of an immense crowd and mass attendance supports >=50; no numeric bound.

protester_violence.summary: Article does not establish protester violence; remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The article reports support and thanks directed to prior actions; it does not document a state response to this 28 January meeting. All response fields remain unknown.

notes: This is a distinct 28 January physical meeting, two weeks after the 15 January meeting by the same movement, and is not an automatic continuation or merger. LeFaso says supportive gatherings also occurred in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso; identity and relation to reports from those cities remain unresolved. The announced 4 February blood drive is prospective and not coded as a January event. The report is by the same LeFaso reporter as S018; source texts are not independent.
open_questions: Relationship between this Ouahigouya meeting and simultaneous/same-day meetings reported in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso remains unresolved.
The article reports security actions following the 15 January appeal, but independent verification and effects are not established.
Independent review, official baseline and episode reconciliation remain pending.

title: Kossi residents press conference on the Nouna killings
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. LeFaso describes a press conference with journalists and identifies a spokesperson, but does not report the number of attendees or a separate public gathering.

start_date.summary: LeFaso dates the press conference to the afternoon of Wednesday 4 January 2023.

location.summary: Kossi residents based in Bobo-Dioulasso held it there; exact venue not stated.

organizer.summary: Organized by Kossi residents who live in Bobo-Dioulasso.

demands.summary: Spokesperson urges authorities to protect the community and the state to play its role following alleged abuses; account remains attributed.

participants_original.summary: No attendance count or general crowd description reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No evidence that at least 50 people assembled; press/media format is reported, with no number.

protester_violence.summary: Article does not establish violence at the press conference; remains unknown.

state_response.summary: No response to this press conference reported. Prior Nouna deaths occurred before it and are not coded as response or as killings by state forces.

notes: This record is for the 4 January press conference, not the prior 30 December killings. The event source attributes allegations about those deaths to the spokesperson; they remain outside this event’s protest-response fields. A press conference may not be a qualifying public mass assembly, and no participant count or open public format is established.
open_questions: Whether this press conference drew at least 50 participants or was a broader public assembly is unknown.
The spokesperson’s allegations and any state response are not independently corroborated in this source.
Independent review, official baseline and episode reconciliation remain pending.
